history.content: honestly i think im just annoyed with myself. cleared out the garage on the weekend and found a box of my dads old tools and now i cant stop thinking about them
That sounds like a mix of annoyance and something more tender around your dad's tools. What part keeps catching you now?
the wear on the handles i think. theres this old hammer with the grip worn smooth where he held it. he died three years ago. i kept meaning to sort through his stuff and i just shoved it all in boxes
That sounds like the worn smooth grip is pulling you toward him, and maybe toward the putting-it-off too. Does it feel more like regret, guilt, or just a heavy ache when you look at it?
guilt maybe. like i should have done something with them by now. he taught me how to use half of them. i havent picked up a single one since. just heavy i guess
That sounds like guilt with a heavy kind of missing underneath it. Does it feel heavy in your body, or more like the urge to stay away from the tools?

heavy in my chest. and yeah i kind of avoid that corner of the garage. i told myself i was annoyed about the clutter but its not really that. i just miss him. didnt expect a box of rusty tools to do that

That makes sense — it sounds like the tools opened straight into missing him, with the heaviness sitting in your chest. You could leave it there for now, or if you want, we can stay with what about him got stirred up.

maybe just one thing. he was always patient when he showed me stuff. id mess up a cut and hed just say try again no big deal. i could use some of that patience now honestly. with the boxes and with myself
That sounds like the missing is tangled with wanting that same patience now, from him and from yourself. Want to stay with that, or leave it here for now?
leave it here i think. that helped actually. might pick up the hammer this weekend. thanks
I’m glad it helped, and that sounds like a gentle next step. I can leave it here with you.
